key_insight: A benchmark can measure the wrong skill: PigAirwayPressure asks classifiers to identify which of 52 pigs produced a recording, although the original experiment investigated hemorrhage detection. The paper questions whether standard time-series benchmarks reflect the problems practitioners actually need to solve.
problem_solved: Addresses the risk of treating performance on the UCR Time Series Classification Archive as evidence of real-world usefulness without examining what its classification labels represent.
method: Examines the alignment between benchmark classification tasks and the scientific goals behind their source data.
Uses PigAirwayPressure to illustrate the contrast between identifying individual animals and detecting a critical physiological condition.
impact: Practitioners should check what benchmark labels actually measure before interpreting model rankings as practical progress. Strong subject-identification performance does not establish effectiveness at detecting hemorrhage.

paper_title: Fifty-Two Shades of Pig: What the UCR Archive Really Asks Classifiers to Do
paper_authors: Omar Swelam, Jaris Küken, Shi Bin Hoo, Frank Hutter, Lennart Purucker
